questions.question: During the colonial rule in India, which hill station became the official residence of the commander-in-chief of the Indian Army?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shimla.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **During colonial rule in India, Shimla became the official residence of the commander-in-chief of the Indian Army.**
 
• The establishment and settlement of hill stations were initially linked to the needs of the British Army.
 
• Hill stations were strategically important for dispersing troops, guarding borders, and launching campaigns against enemy rulers.
 
• In this sequence, **Shimla was established during the Gorkha War (1815-16).**
 
• Since the hill stations were similar to the cold climate of Europe, so hill stations became an attractive destination for the Viceroys during the summer months.
 
• **In 1864,** the** Viceroy John Lawrence **officially transferred his council to Shimla, making it a practice to relocate the capitals during the hot season.
 
• Shimla also became the official residence of the Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Army.
 
• These hill stations were also developed as sanitariums, i.e. places where soldiers could be sent for rest and recovery from illnesses, and over the years they became cantonments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The interest of the British in** Mount Abu Hill Station** came during the Anglo-Maratha War of 1818.
 
• **Darjeeling **was snatched from the rulers of Sikkim by the **British in 1835.**

questions.question: In which of the following years did the Opium Act come into force to regulate the cultivation of opium poppy and manufacture of opium?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1857.**__

__
 
• The **Opium Act 1857** came into force to regulate the cultivation of opium poppy and manufacture of opium.
 
• India as a monopoly of Govt. of India **Opium Act 1857 **regulated the sale of opium and poppy heads, their inter-state import & export.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• To consolidate and amend the law relating to narcotic drugs.
 
• To make stringent provisions to control and regulate the operation relating to narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.
 
• To considerably enhance penalties, particularly for trafficking offenses.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of Amphibia class of animals?

options.text: The amphibian skin is moist (without scales).
In amphibians, a tympanum represents the ear.
The amphibians can live in aquatic as well as terrestrial habitats.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amphibians' eyes are without eyelids.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Amphibians are those animals who are found both on land & water i.e. amphibians can live in aquatic as well as terrestrial habitats. **Hence, statement 4 is correct.**
 
• In Amphibians, respiration takes place through the gill, skin, and lungs.
 
 
• ​During hibernation, frogs respire through the skin. 
 
 
 
• They have porous skin that requires moisture. i.e the amphibian skin is moist (without scales). **Hence, **statement ** 1 is correct.**
 
• They have three-chambered hearts, two auricles, and one ventricle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Frogs have two transparent eyelids, one on the bottom, one on the top, and a third semi-transparent eyelid called the nictitating membrane.
 
• Amphibians' eyes have eyelids. **Hence, statement 3 is not a characteristic of the Amphibia class of animals.**
 
• The body of Amphibians is divided into the head and trunk.
 
• In amphibians, a tympanum is located just behind the eye but it does not process sound waves; it simply transmits them to the inner parts of the amphibian's ear which are protected from the entry of water and other foreign objects. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
 
 
• The tympanum is a large external oval-shaped membrane made up of non-glandular skin.
 
 
 
• They are cold-blooded.
 
• Examples of Amphibians are Frog, Necturus, Salamander, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/197f85f3f2286586ed1f6625ae6d4a290034b4e882c70821a65c1709becbe738.png]

questions.question: When was the Majority Act, which defines the age of the majority of Indian citizens, passed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1875.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The **Majority Act of 1875 **is divided into two sections:
 
• **Section 3(1)**
 
 
• Every person domiciled in India shall attain the age of majority on completion of 18 years and not before. 
 
• Unless a particular personal law specifies otherwise, every person domiciled in India is deemed to have attained majority upon completion of 18 years of age. 
 
 
 
• **Section 3(2)**
 
 
• In computing the age of any person, the day on which he was born is to be included as a whole day and he shall be deemed to have attained majority at the beginning of the eighteenth anniversary of that day. 
 
• But if the child born is appointed a guardian or he/she is under the court of wards then he/she attains majority after his completion of 21 years of age.

questions.question: Which of the following dynasties ruled from Thaneshwar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pushyabhuti.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Pushyabhuti dynasty **also known as the **Vardhana dynasty** ruled parts of northern India **during the 6th and 7th centuries.**
 
• The Pushyabhuti Dynasty (c. 500 CE - 647 CE) rose after the downfall of the Gupta Empire (3rd century CE - 6th century CE) in the 6th century CE in northern India.
 
• The core area of their kingdom was situated in what is now the state of Haryana in India with the capital at Sthanishvara or Thaneshwar.
 
• The dynasty reached its zenith under its last ruler **Harsha Vardhana. **He ruled from 606 AD to 647 AD.
 
• The capital of Harshavardhana's Empire was Kannuaj. 
 
• His empire covered much of **north and north-western India.**
 
• His Empire extended from Punjab to northern Orissa and **from the Himalayas** to the** bank of the Narmada River.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Maurya**__

 __
 
• Three important rulers of the Maurya dynasty were
 
 
• **Chandragupta.**
 
• **Bindusara.**
 
• **Ashoka.**
 
 
 
• Chandragupta dethroned the last Nanda ruler Dhanananda and occupied the **Patliputra** in 322 BC.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya was succeeded by his son Bindusara.
 
• Ashoka was the son of Bindusara. 
 
 
 
• Rashtrakutas__
 __
 
• They ruled **parts of South India** from the 8th to the 10th century CE.
 
• Their kingdom included the modern state of Karnataka in its entirety along with parts of the current Indian states of Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Maharashtra, and Gujarat. 
 
• They were **originally known** to be the **feudatories of the Western Chalukyas of Vatapi.**
 
• **Dhantidurga** was the founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty as he defeated Chalukyas of Badami.
 
• The **worship of Shiva **and **Vishnu** was **popular** during the Rashtrakuta reign.
 
 
 
• **Satavahana**__
 
 
• The Satavahana dynasty was an ancient Indian dynasty that was based in the Deccan region.
 
• They ruled between the 2nd century BCE and the early 3rd century CE.
 
• The capital cities of the dynasty were Amaravati and Pratishthana.
 
• Simuka was the founder of the dynasty.
 
• Pulumavi IV was the last ruler of the Satavahana kingdom.

questions.question: The unit of electrical resistance in the meter-kilogram-second system is called a/an ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ohm**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **unit **of **electrical resistance** in the** meter-kilogram-second system** is called **ohm.**
 
• **Electrical resistance **is the characteristic of a **material** that **slows electron flow.**
 
 
• ​**Resistance** is represented by the symbol **R**.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **watt** is the SI unit of power**. **It is a** scientific unit **of **electrical power** that is commonly used to **describe the rate of energy consumption** of an **electrical appliance.**

 
 
• **One watt **is the **power equal** to** one joule **of **energy per second.**
 
 
 
• **​Ampere (A) **represents the **number of electrons **that **flow past a point** in a** circuit in one second. It is the SI unit of electric current.**
 
• The **volt **is the derived unit for **electric potential, electric potential difference, and electromotive force**. It is named after the Italian physicist Alessandro Volta.

questions.question: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi make his first major public appearance in India?

__
 
• **Gandhi** got an **invitation** to the **opening ceremony of Banaras Hindu University(BHU) in 1916**.
 
• Many eminent speakers were **invited as guests** and Gandhi was one of them. 
 
• He **addressed the gathering** where **most of the audience were young** people.
 
• This was the **first public appearance of Mahatma Gandhi**.
 
• Madan Mohan Malaviya was one of the founders of BHU. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __

 __

• Gandhi stood behind the farmers' cause and won concessions.

• **1918**__

questions.question: The Bibi Ka Maqbara, the burial place of Aurangzeb’s wife, Rabia-ud-Durrani near Aurangabad city is an imitation of which of the following monuments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Taj Mahal at Agra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bibi Ka Maqbara **__

 __
 
• Bibi Ka Maqbara in **Aurangabad** is a magnificent mausoleum.
 
• It exhibits exceptional architectural beauty. 
 
• It was constructed in** 1668-69 by Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.**
 
• It was constructed as a memorial to his first wife **Rabia-Ul-Daurani aka Dilras Banu Begum.**
 
• It is a fine example of Mughal architecture.
 
• **Bibi Ka Maqbara** is located on a raised square platform that is 19 feet high. 
 
• Four minarets, each with a height of 72 feet and featuring 144 stairs that lead to the top, stand at the four corners of the platform.
 
• There is also a mosque to the west of the structure. 
 
• The portion up to the dado level and the dome are constructed in marble while the rest of the tomb features basaltic trap construction.
 
• Bibi Ka Maqbara is one of the finest structures and a top tourist attraction in Aurangabad. 
 
• **It is often referred to as the Dakkhani Taj or the Taj of Deccan as it was modeled on the iconic Taj Mahal.** 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jama Masjid at Delhi** - The Masjid-i Jehan-Numa, commonly known as the Jama Masjid of Delhi, is one of the largest mosques in India. It was built by the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan between 1650 and 1656.
 
• **Safdarjung's Tomb at New Delhi** - Safdarjung's Tomb is a sandstone and marble mausoleum in Delhi, India. It was built in 1754 in the late Mughal Empire style for Nawab Safdarjung. 
 
• **Humayun's Tomb at New Delhi** - Humayun's tomb is the tomb of the Mughal Emperor Humayun in Delhi, India. The tomb was commissioned by Humayun's chief consort, Empress Bega Begum, in 1558, and designed by Mirak Mirza Ghiyas and his son, Sayyid Muhammad, Persian architects chosen by her.

questions.question: The thickness of the ozone in a column of air from the ground to the top of the atmosphere is measured in terms of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Dobson Units (DU)__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **thickness** of the **ozone **in a **column** of **air** from the **ground **to the **top **of the** atmosphere **is measured in terms of** the Dobson Unit (DU).**
 
• **Dobson Unit (DU)** is defined to be **0.01mm thickness** at **STP - (zero degrees Celcius and 1 atm press)**, A **slab of 3mm **corresponds to **300 DU.**
 
• **Ozone** forms a** layer** in the **stratosphere,** **thinnest **in the **tropics (around the equator)** and **denser** towards** the poles.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• A **carat **is a unit of weight used to measure the size of a gemstone such as a diamond. A **karat **is a measurement indicating the proportion of gold in an alloy out of 24 parts, so 18K gold is 18/24 parts gold. **However, the use of carat (in place of karat) to indicate the fineness of gold is also considered acceptable.**
 
• A **micrometer**, sometimes known as a micrometer screw gauge, is a device incorporating a calibrated screw widely used for accurate measurement of components in mechanical engineering and machining as well as most mechanical trades, along with other metrological instruments such as dial, vernier, and digital calipers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Ozone layer** is the layer in **Earth's atmosphere** which** contains** a relatively **high concentration of ozone (O₃). **This layer **absorbs 97-99%** of the **sun's high-frequency ultraviolet light**, which is potentially **damaging to life on earth.**

questions.question: The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with which of the following?

options.text: Allotment of seats in the State Legislative Council
Allotment of seats in Rajya Sabha
Allotment of seats in Lok Sabha
Allotment of seats in the State Legislative Assembly

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allotment of seats in Rajya Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the Allotment of seats in Rajya Sabha from each state and some union territory.
 
• According to **Article 80** of the Indian Constitution, the potential sitting capacity of the Rajya Sabha is **250 (238 elected, 12 appointed).**
 
• **Uttar Pradesh** has the **maximum number of 31 seats **in the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Only **three Union Territories of Delhi (3 seats), Jammu and Kashmir (4 seats), and Puducherry (1 seat) **have Rajya Sabha seats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Schedule of the Indian Constitution **
 **Subject Matter**
 
 

 First Schedule
 Names of the States and Union Territories with their territorial jurisdiction.
 
 

 Second Schedule
 Provisions relating to the emoluments, allowances, privileges.
 
 

 Third Schedule
 Forms of Oaths or Affirmations.
 
 

 **Fourth Schedule**
 **Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to the states and the union territories.**
 
 

 Fifth Schedule
 Provisions relating to the administration and control of scheduled areas and scheduled tribes.
 
 

 Sixth Schedule
 Provisions relating to the administration of tribal areas in the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.
 
 

 Seventh Schedule
 Division of powers between the Union and the States in terms of List I (Union List), List II (State List), and List III (Concurrent List).
 
 

 Eighth Schedule
 Languages recognized by the Constitution.
 
 

 Ninth Schedule
 Acts and Regulations of the state legislatures dealing with land reforms and the abolition of the zamindari system and of the Parliament dealing with other matters.
 
 

 Tenth Schedule
 Provisions relating to disqualification of the members of Parliament and State Legislatures on the ground of defection.
 
 

 Eleventh Schedule
 Specifies the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats.
 
 

 Twelfth Schedule
 Specifies the powers, authority, and responsibilities of Municipalities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

 
• Nemonic for twelve schedules of Indian constitution: 
 
• **'TEARS OF OLD PM'**
 
 
• **T**erritory,** E**molument, **A**ffirmation, **R**ajya sabha seat allocation, **S**chedule Area, **O**ther schedule areas, **F**ederal division of tasks, **O**fficial languages, **L**and reforms, **D**efection, **P**anchayat raj, **M**unicipality.

questions.question: ‘Natya Shastra’, a Sanskrit Hindu text that deals with performing arts, elucidates several gestures of Indian classical dances and according to it, Mohiniyattam is which of the following form of dances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lasya**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **‘Natya Shastra’,** a **Sanskrit Hindu** text that deals with **performing arts, elucidates several gestures** of** Indian classical dances **and according to it, **Mohiniyattam** is a **Lasya** form of dance.
 
• After the demon **‘Tripurasur’** was killed by **Lord Shiva**, he **danced in rage** i.e.** Tandava.** Then to pacify and please him, **Goddess Uma **performed a soft and Shringarik dance, which is called** ‘Lasya’.**
 
• **Mohiniyattam or Mohiniattam **is a **classical dance** form that originated in **Kerala.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhava **- (in Indian dance and other performing arts) is the emotion or mood conveyed by a performer.
 
• A **rasa** __is a sentiment or emotion evoked in each member of the audience by the art.
 
• **Tandava** also known as **Tandava Natyam**, is a divine dance performed by the **Hindu god Shiva.**

questions.question: Who among the following got Padma Vibhushan Award 2022 under the Public Affairs category?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalyan Singh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

questions.question: Kargil Vijay Diwas is celebrated on ________ every year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**26th July**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kargil Vijay Diwas**__

 __
 
• Every year **26th July** is observed as the **Kargil Vijay Diwas.**
 
• It is in the memory of the recapture of the Kargil hills after defeating the Pakistani troops in the Kargil district in the Ladakh division.
 
• The mission was named 'Operation Vijay' by the Indian Army, while the Air Force named it 'Operation Safed Sagar'.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Operation Vijay**__

 
 
• In the year **1999,** India and Pakistan signed the **Lahore Agreement** to mutually resolve the Kashmir issue in a peaceful manner.
 
• However, the Pakistani troops began infiltrating toward the Indian side of the Line of Control (LoC) under **Operation Badr**, hoping to cut off Indian Troops in Siachen. 
 
• Indian Army responded by launching **Operation Vijay**.
 
• On **3rd May 1999**, Pakistan started this war when it had infiltrated into the high altitudes in the rocky mountainous region of Kargil with around 5000 soldiers and captured it.
 
• When the Indian Government got the information about it,** ‘Operation Vijay’** was launched by the Indian army to throw back the intruders who had treacherously occupied Indian Territory.

questions.question: The ‘Reporters Without Borders’, a not-for-profit body published the 'World Press Freedom Index, 2021' which ranked 180 countries. What is the rank of India in this index?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**142.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **‘Reporters Without Borders’**, a not-for-profit body published the 'World Press Freedom Index, 2021' which ranked 180 countries.

 
 
• **India is ranked 142 in this index.**
 
 
 
• In the year 2020, India was ranked 142.
 
• India is classified as one of the 'bad' countries for journalism and is said to be one of the most dangerous countries for journalists who are trying to do their jobs properly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Norway topped for the fifth year **in a row, followed by **Finland and Denmark.**
 
• **Eritrea** is at the **bottom **while China ranks 177, and is only behind** North Korea at 179 **and Turkmenistan at 178.
 
• India's neighboring countries rank in the index;
 
 
• Bhutan - 65
 
• Nepal -106
 
• Sri Lanka -127
 
• Pakistan - 145
 
• China - 177
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Press Freedom Index**__

 
 
• It is published every year since 2002 by Reporters Without Borders (Reporters Sans Frontieres).
 
 
• Reporters Without Borders (RWB) is located in **Paris.**
 
 
 
• The index ranks countries and regions according to **the level of freedom available to journalists there.**
 
• It is not an indicator of the quality of journalism.

questions.question: Which of the following schemes was launched to raise the overall status of the girl-child and bring about a positive change in family and community attitudes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Balika Samriddhi Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Balika Samriddhi Yojana**__

 
 
• The scheme of **Balika Samriddhi Yojana was launched on 2nd October 1997.**
 
• **The objective of the scheme was to raise the overall status of the girl-child and bring about a positive change in family and community attitudes.**
 
• The scheme covers two girls' children born on or after 15th August 1997 in a family living below the poverty line as defined by the Government of India.
 
• A one-time grant of** Rs.500/- **is given to a mother giving birth to a girl child of B.P.L. families.
 
• Coverage of beneficiaries is 12357 girl child, as till date. (April 2022)

questions.question: Which one of the following cities of the Indus Valley Civilization was mostly devoted to craft production, including bead making, shell shearing, metalworking, seal making, and weight-making?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chanhudaro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chanhudaro**__

 
 
• It is a Harappan site.
 
• It was a tiny settlement as compared to other Harappan sites such as Mohenjodaro.
 
• **The site was almost exclusively devoted to craft production, including bead-making, shell-cutting, metal-working, seal-making, and weight-making**.
 
• The variety of materials used to make beads was remarkable.
 
• It contained stones like carnelian (of a beautiful red color), jasper, crystal, quartz, and steatite, metals like copper, bronze, and gold, and shell, faience, and terracotta or burnt clay.
 
• Some beads were made of two or more stones, cemented together, some of stones with gold caps.
 
• The shapes were numerous – disc-shaped, cylindrical, spherical, barrel-shaped, segmented.
 
• Some were decorated by incising or painting, and some had designs etched onto them.
 
• Specialized drills have been found at Chanhudaro.
 
• **There is no evidence of Iron ore extraction from Chanhudaro.**
